observe: The colour was immediately of interest, it did not fit the SRM scale at all, there are white bubbles with a light red hue. Upon opening the bottle, it was corked, immitting a slight cherry odur and some notable gas. It is a reddish almost a little purple colour. LIke a ruby red.
aroma: The first smell notes are vinegar, like a red wine vinegar and some acidic sweetness. The cherries come through and seem more sour. There is the smell of some barrel age or some age in general.
taste:
Immiediately hit with a pungent sourness, but very little bitterness. It does have a vinegar quality to it. The cherry does come through, but it comes through very tart and sour, rather than light and crisp.
Im not really getting a lot of the bread characteristics I would assume to find in a beer, it comes through more wine like with very in your face bold flavours. The carbonation is rather mild, it has a more bold heavy body and is much more sticky and viscous. There is a little dryness, some tannins from leaving the wine to sit in the mouth. There is the taste of some age in the barrel, a bit of woodiness and that barrel taste comes through for sure.
I am getting some sort of alcoholic almond liquor flavour coming through, like an amaretto cookie

observe: Immediately visually there is a dark high SRM, somewhat opaque near the bottom but difficult to tell. The head remains for quite some time, and the beer has a layer of light brown bubbles that are quite large.
aroma: Upon smelling there is an immediate caramel and bready note, very intense flavours off the bat. Almost like a heavy caramel dessert with a light crispenss to it with some sort of fruity undertones presenting themselves. I am also smelling some
taste: Immediately on the palette this beer is very rich, there is an immediate smokiness and some deep burnt flavours and some caramel. I want to lean towards a creme brulee, but at a very extreme level. There are some molasses and other deep sugary notes, but without the extreme smokiness and bitterness I would expect from something like a stout.

observe: Opaque golden honey like colour, white foam head that dissipates (note I did mess up and leave this in the freezer overnight)
aroma: smells like a wittbier, there are very fruity floral aromas to it with some bready malts, think hibiscus pungent fruitiness and honey like aroma. Could be a wheat bear yeast? Going back and smelling again, smokiness comes through a bit too?
taste:
big alcohol flavour with hop bitterness at the back of the mouth. Maybe a harder water since this doesn’t coat the mouth like a wittbier from Germany or Pilsner would. Very bitter.
I am getting a big wood flavour, and a lot of alcohol and some sweetness. It leans towards a very hoppy bitterness, very piney, earthy and herbal. Maybe a little spice on the palette as well, like a black pepper. Maltiness is prominent, with a light bready taste almost like the whites of bread, not as toasty

observe: orange, not a hazy or amber colour but a proper orange colour, hazy throughout, no head on pour, mild carbonation. Looks viscous
aroma: citrus (orange lemon lime), a bit of yeast and maybe some citrusy hops, a smell of vinegar (white wine vinegar) as well. It does smell like rainbow sherbert ice cream for sure
taste: immediately fruit forward flavour, hop bitterness at the back of the palett and lots of fruits (green apple, pineapple, citrus fruits). There is a lot of sweetness as well, and some sourness. The mouth feel is dry and sticky after drinking. It has a candy limoncello sickly sweet flavour.

observe: lighter semi hazy but relatively clear, must be a lower SRM, foamy head, big bubbles that hold a big foamy head
aroma: bready, lager smell, not a big hop charerteristic. Caramel, sugar and very bread forward smell, the smell of malted barley is definitely the primary scent
taste: very big hop floral flavour on the palette, honey like sweetness and there is very light hop bitterness. Crisp on the palette, a little bit more medium boldness, this is a very alcoholic beer, that alcohol flavour is very forward .

observe: fairly light amber colour, honey, light head presence, fairly opaque, some light bubbles. There is decent head retention on the beer, with some nice lacing appearing on the glass as well.
aroma: yeast smell immediately, very heavy bread flavour. Some light piney hop smell but not very heavy. The malt comes forward and is very pronounced with this beer and I do find there is a light caramel swell or something sweet on the nose as well.
taste: honey, sticky and a very big bread forward smell. Crisp with an apple flavour, some molasses. Hop bitterness back of palette. A big thing to note after a few sips is a big dried fruit taste as well, some raison or dried figs being very pronounced. Overall a very malty fruit forward beer with a lot of warmth.

observe: A very light refreshing Lager, foamy head with lots of carbonation. Very low on the srm, very opaque and it looks crisp. The head remains after a while. A light straw appearance with a lot of carbonation
aroma: sweet aroma, not a very big hop profile, more characteristic of a large commercial beer. I am more getting a commercial lager aroma here with some light breadiness and a little bit of light sweet caramel, maybe some light apple notes like a Gala or Fuji apple.
taste: Once again, there is a very light breadiness, but I unfortunately could not taste much of the hops on this beer. There was a bit of bitterness towards the back of the palette, but overall I found the beer crisp and refreshing (some nice Gala Apple notes)

observe: large foamy head, dark colour, hazy, a little bit darker head. In the light a bit chestnutty and brown, with some nice head retention.
aroma: Molasses, smoky, burnt bread or some toastier bread (I did smell this while near a campfire). Not really grabbing any weitbier smells, the malt takes over
taste: molasses, malted barley flavour, caramels and some burnt cheesecake, like a basque cheesecake It`s rather viscous, thicker of a beer, medium to bold bodied, some dry mouth feel, not really any bitterness. I was lookin for some Weitbier characteristics but that dark malt overpowers quite a bit of it, I can really try searching for some banana/bubblegum flavours and aromas, but I am just getting that malty nuttiness, breadiness and caramel flavours, which in themselves are quite welcome.

beerName: St Bernardus Unfiltered Helles Weihenstephan : Kombine 2025
observe: cloudy, amber colour, large foamy head, big foamy head that remains for a while. After sitting a bit, there is some light lacing and decent head retention as well.
aroma: Very metallic smell on the nose, smells like blood to me? Yeast smell, and some bread and fermentation. There is a bit of Hopps on the initial pour where it had a bit of fruitiness and floral characteristics. Something like a lavender. A bit of a honey smell as well
taste: honey flavour right away on the palette, a sweet pastry flavour. Breathing out after a taste, it has a big white bread flavour too. Some subtle floral hop flavours on the palette as well, this one being citrusy on the palette. Dryness on the mouth as well

observe: dark caramel colour, foam on the top that quickly dissipates. Cloudy, dark brown with a bit of orange
aroma: dried fruits, fruit leathers, fruity aroma, very sweet caramel and there are deep malty characteristics. Like a sweet caramel dessert think of a sticky toffee pudding with dates
taste: that’s a lot of alcohol, kind of what I think gasoline would taste like. It is very sweet with a malty characteristic, medium bodied, wine characteristics, I believe I can taste some wood or barrel aging. On the taste I get a lot of warmth and a warm alcohol burn near my nose and the top of the pallet. Metallic flavours as well, something like copper you get from a penny. Medium bodied, sticky mouth feel, with a warm burn, but an astringent aftertaste
